_baseline_note: E008: BERT-small T cell, f0, seed 0, eval every 500, best checkpoint by val AUC (default). Val AUC peaked at iter 500 (70.14) and decayed monotonically; test llm AP 84.96, below E007's 88.58 whose AUC-selected checkpoint was iter 1500. So val AUC and test llm AP move in opposite directions over training on this cell. Val 7-bit mAP in the E008 log peaked at iter 2000. BERT-base T_base: 91.60.

factor._note: absent = trainer default 'AUC' (config.get('select_metric','AUC')). 'mAP' = best checkpoint / early stop by validation 7-bit mAP instead of binary AUC. Six of the seven val bits are invisible to T and near chance, so the val mAP variation is driven by the llm bit; it is a noisy but aligned proxy for the test target. Suite flag --select-metric mAP; same 500-iter grid, LR, iters, patience count as E008.

hypothesis: Selecting the checkpoint by val mAP instead of val AUC picks a later, attribution-better checkpoint (around iter 2000 on the E008 grid) and lifts f0 test llm AP above E007's 88.58, target >= 91.0 (BERT-base 91.60): the gap of the small BERTs to BERT-base is a checkpoint-selection artifact, not capacity. AUC may drop toward E007's 67.88 since the early AUC peak is no longer selected.
_success_note: test.mAP == llm_textgen AP (nkeep=1). Verdict is strict-sign vs E008 (84.96); the pre-registered bar is E007's 88.58 and the user's target 91.0. If > 88.58 but < 91.0: selection helps, remaining gap is capacity/LR. If <= 84.96: val 7-bit mAP is too noisy a selector; next would be a visible-bits-only val mAP.
